themes.name: Social Media Platforms
themes.description: Online services enabling user-generated content creation, sharing, and networking, fostering digital communities and facilitating real-time social interaction.

linked_companies.name: SNAP INC - A
linked_companies.description: Operates a visual messaging and multimedia sharing application that connects users through ephemeral content, augmented reality experiences, and curated media, functioning as a core platform for digital social interaction.
linked_companies.evidence: Snap operates as a pure-play digital platform, with 100% of its recent $1.53 billion quarterly revenue generated directly from advertising and Snapchat+ subscriptions. Despite management's framing of the application as a communication-first tool rather than traditional social media, the platform's core functionality relies entirely on user-generated content, digital communities, and a massive network of 956 million monthly active users. To sustain this entrenched competitive moat, the company directs multi-billion dollar capital and infrastructure investments toward expanding ecosystem features like Creator Subscriptions and Spotlight, which recently drove a 62% global increase in shares and reposts.

linked_companies.name: PINTEREST INC- CLASS A
linked_companies.description: Operates a visual discovery and image-sharing platform that enables users to curate, save, and interact with digital content, driving user engagement and content discovery within the broader social media ecosystem.
linked_companies.evidence: Pinterest functions as a visual discovery and digital community platform, engaging 631 million global monthly active users to curate and interact with user-generated content. The company explicitly positions itself as a positive alternative to traditional social media by competing on its safety record and targeting younger demographics, with Gen Z now representing over half of its user base. This audience provides the foundational engagement signals required to power Pinterest's targeted advertising engine, which generates all of the company's revenue. To support continuous user growth and platform health, the company directs research and development spending toward system infrastructure, content personalization, and moderation operations.

linked_companies.name: REDDIT INC-CL A
linked_companies.description: Operates a community-driven platform consisting of thousands of user-generated forums where individuals create, share, and curate content, facilitating global online interaction and digital engagement.
linked_companies.evidence: Reddit operates as a pure-play social media platform centered on user-generated content and community-enforced rules across hundreds of thousands of subreddits. The company's organizational structure is entirely dedicated to this ecosystem, expanding its reach to 444 million Weekly Active Users and generating $549 million in fourth-quarter 2025 advertising revenue directly from on-platform engagement. To advance global user retention and community diversification, leadership is deploying specialized tools like 'Reddit Pro' for publishers alongside over $584 million in recent research and development investments to enhance the core application experience.

linked_companies.name: RUM GROUP INC
linked_companies.description: Provides a video-sharing and social media platform that enables creators to host, stream, and monetize content while fostering community engagement and digital discourse.
linked_companies.evidence: Rumble operates a user-generated video platform driven by a creator ecosystem and follower engagement, totaling 56 million Monthly Active Users in the second quarter of 2026. The company is accelerating the Rumble Shorts feed to increase interaction and plans to roll out native advertising features for creators comparable to Facebook, X, and Instagram. By generating revenue through audience monetization and offering networking tools such as tipping and subscriber communities, the platform relies explicitly on social media mechanics to sustain its core operations.

linked_companies.name: TRUMP MEDIA & TECHNOLOGY GRO
linked_companies.description: Develops and operates a proprietary social networking platform offering microblogging, multimedia sharing, and video streaming capabilities as an alternative to mainstream social media networks.
linked_companies.evidence: TMTG's operations are deeply rooted in the social media industry through its flagship product, Truth Social, an open network built to operate independently of Big Tech infrastructure. Expanding this platform is the company's primary strategic initiative for driving advertising revenue, managed directly by CEO Kevin McGurn under a dedicated "Media" reporting segment. To support this foundational business model, the company actively invests in its proprietary ecosystem, recently allocating $8.4 million in quarterly research and development to deploy cross-platform applications and community features like direct messaging and customized feeds.

themes.name: Digital Marketing Technology
themes.description: Platforms enabling targeted online advertising and digital customer engagement through data analytics and AI-driven personalization.

linked_companies.name: TRADE DESK INC/THE -CLASS A
linked_companies.description: Operates a cloud-based demand-side platform that enables advertising buyers to programmatically create, manage, and optimize data-driven digital marketing campaigns across diverse media channels and formats.
linked_companies.evidence: The Trade Desk operates as a pure-play provider of digital marketing technology, generating the entirety of its revenue through an objective media buying platform that enables clients to execute targeted online advertising. Recent product development centers on AI-fueled decisioning tools, highlighted by the Q2 2026 rollout of "Audience Unlimited," which utilizes a data marketplace capturing over 80% of U.S. retail sales to automate audience selection, reduce media costs, and drive higher campaign conversion rates. To maintain this core advertising architecture, the company directs its operating expenses and capital investments toward expanding platform hosting capabilities, advancing its agentic AI software, Kokai, and aligning its workforce to support data-driven digital spend activation.

linked_companies.name: ALPHABET INC-CL A
linked_companies.description: Operates a comprehensive suite of digital advertising and marketing platforms, providing search, programmatic, and analytics solutions that enable businesses to target audiences, manage campaigns, and measure performance across the internet.
linked_companies.evidence: Alphabet's engagement with Digital Marketing Technology relies on its foundational ad platforms, which generate roughly 70% of the company's total revenue, recently totaling $77.3 billion. During the second quarter of 2026, the company accelerated the deployment of its proprietary Gemini AI models across its entire ads infrastructure, resulting in a nearly 10% improvement in ad relevance. This integration directly powers core advertiser tools like Smart Bidding, Performance Max—which now captures over 30% of customer search spend—and the newly upgraded AI Max tool. By leveraging these AI-enabled platforms to deliver targeted, high-return campaigns for marketers, Alphabet solidifies advertising technology as its primary economic engine.

linked_companies.name: APPLOVIN CORP-CLASS A
linked_companies.description: Provides an end-to-end software platform utilizing advanced machine learning algorithms to enable developers to automate, optimize, and measure their digital marketing and monetization campaigns.
linked_companies.evidence: AppLovin operates as a pure-play digital marketing technology provider, leveraging its AI-powered Axon platform to optimize return on ad spend and automate targeted customer acquisition campaigns. The company's rollout of Axon 2.0 and continuous model upgrades have increased advertiser scale and campaign performance, directly driving 1.84 billion dollars in recent quarterly revenue and facilitating expansion into global consumer verticals. Backed by dedicated engineering teams, AppLovin continues to broaden its ecosystem by introducing global self-serve advertising capabilities and integrating its MAX mediation auction with the Adjust analytics platform to deliver an end-to-end suite for marketing attribution and campaign management.

linked_companies.name: DOUBLEVERIFY HOLDINGS INC
linked_companies.description: Provides a software platform for digital media measurement and analytics, equipping advertisers with brand safety, fraud prevention, and viewability tools to optimize the performance and quality of their digital marketing campaigns.
linked_companies.evidence: DoubleVerify operates as a digital marketing technology provider, generating its $180.8 million first-quarter 2026 revenue entirely through an AI-driven media effectiveness platform that validates ad inventory and measures advertising outcomes. The company's proprietary Media AdVantage Platform (MAP) integrates independent verification with real-time optimization, utilizing tools like Rockerbox Relay to send attribution results directly to ecosystems such as Meta as targeted optimization signals. To scale these advertising analytics capabilities, the company dedicates its 1,231-employee workforce and directs its capital investments toward product innovation, including $45.4 million in quarterly research and development. By processing hundreds of terabytes of proprietary advertising data across trillions of transactions, these technologies allow global brands to dynamically evaluate and improve campaign suitability and viewability across programmatic, social media, and connected TV channels.

linked_companies.name: KLAVIYO INC-A
linked_companies.description: Powers digital marketing strategies through a cloud-based automation platform that unifies first-party customer data to deliver targeted email, SMS, and push notifications for e-commerce brands.
linked_companies.evidence: Klaviyo operates fundamentally as an AI-native B2C CRM and centralized digital marketing technology stack, generating nearly all of its revenue—including $358 million in its most recently reported quarter—through automated campaign creation and customer data consolidation. The company continuously expands its marketing ecosystem, recently deploying over 75 new features in a single quarter, launching beta integrations for Google Search and Ads, and utilizing its 'Composer' agent to drive one-to-one personalization. The platform's efficacy is validated by top-tier industry recognition, securing the highest customer satisfaction score in a recent Forrester Wave while delivering a 10x revenue-per-message ROI for automated workflows compared to static campaigns. To support this pure-play digital engagement focus across a global base of over 196,000 businesses, Klaviyo dedicates its engineering workforce and major R&D investments toward optimizing autonomous, omnichannel marketing across email, text, and WhatsApp.

themes.name: Artificial Intelligence
themes.description: The science of creating machines and systems capable of performing tasks that typically require human intelligence, such as learning, reasoning, and problem-solving.

linked_companies.name: MICROSOFT CORP
linked_companies.description: Drives the advancement of artificial intelligence by integrating generative AI capabilities across its enterprise software ecosystem and providing scalable cloud infrastructure to support advanced model training and deployment.
linked_companies.evidence: Microsoft's engagement with Artificial Intelligence centers on a dedicated AI business segment that recently reached a $37 billion annualized revenue run rate, expanding 123% to represent over 11% of the company's total revenue. To sustain this shift toward 'agentic' computing platforms, management is directing tens of billions in capital expenditures and increased R&D operating expenses specifically toward AI compute capacity, model training, and specialized talent acquisition. This extensive infrastructure build-out supports foundational models from its long-term OpenAI partnership, enabling the universal integration of AI tools like Copilot and Work IQ across Microsoft's consumer and enterprise software ecosystems.

linked_companies.name: NVIDIA CORP
linked_companies.description: Designs and supplies the foundational graphics processing units and software ecosystems that power artificial intelligence training and inference workloads across global data centers and accelerated computing platforms.
linked_companies.evidence: NVIDIA explicitly defines itself as a data center-scale AI infrastructure company, with its revenue growth primarily driven by Data Center AI solutions that recently accounted for over 92% of total sales. The company's core hardware and edge computing platforms are explicitly optimized for artificial intelligence, directly enabling the deployment of generative, agentic, and physical AI systems. Beyond developing foundational infrastructure, NVIDIA funds the broader global ecosystem through a $17.5 billion investment program targeting early-stage startups and AI model makers, alongside an investment partnership with OpenAI.

linked_companies.name: AMAZON.COM INC
linked_companies.description: Delivers comprehensive cloud-based artificial intelligence services, including foundational models and custom-designed machine learning chips like Trainium and Inferentia, while integrating advanced generative AI capabilities across its e-commerce platform and smart device ecosystem.
linked_companies.evidence: Amazon is directing the majority of its projected $200 billion capital expenditures toward building an end-to-end artificial intelligence ecosystem spanning custom silicon like Trainium to foundation model platforms like Bedrock. This infrastructure powers an expanding enterprise segment, with AWS artificial intelligence workloads surpassing a $15 billion annual revenue run rate by Q2 2026. The company is actively integrating generative technologies across its retail and advertising divisions, deploying over 1,000 internal applications that include the Rufus shopping assistant and Creative Agents. Amazon supplements these proprietary engineering efforts with large-scale external capital deployments, evidenced by partnerships with Anthropic and a $15 billion Series C equity investment in OpenAI.

linked_companies.name: SOUNDHOUND AI INC-A
linked_companies.description: Develops voice artificial intelligence and natural language understanding technologies that power conversational interfaces across automotive, smart device, and customer service applications.
linked_companies.evidence: As a pure-play, "AI-first" enterprise, SoundHound generates 100% of its revenues—reaching $44.2 million in Q1 2026—directly from its Voice, Generative, and Agentic AI platforms. This commercial output is driven by decades of deep tech innovation and data accumulation, anchored by the proprietary Polaris speech recognition foundation model and protected by over 240 granted patents. To further scale its conversational intelligence ecosystem, the company dedicates its entire research and development workforce to AI software advancement and recently deployed nearly $190 million to acquire AI-focused entities including Amelia Holdings and Interactions Corporation.

linked_companies.name: ALPHABET INC-CL A
linked_companies.description: Develops foundational machine learning models, specialized AI infrastructure, and advanced generative AI tools that are deeply integrated across its search, cloud computing, and consumer product ecosystems to drive broader industry innovation.
linked_companies.evidence: Alphabet's full-stack integration of Artificial Intelligence serves as the foundational driver across its entire business ecosystem, natively powering core segments including Search, Cloud, and YouTube. The recent deployment of proprietary technologies, such as Gemini 3.1 Pro models processing 16 billion tokens per minute and custom TPU 8t hardware, has propelled 800% growth in generative AI cloud solutions and secured 350 million paid AI subscriptions. Cementing this structural shift, the company increased its 2026 capital expenditure guidance to between $180 billion and $190 billion strictly for AI compute resources, accompanied by a 26% rise in research and development expenses driven directly by aggressive AI talent acquisition.

themes.name: Generative AI & LLMs
themes.description: AI technologies capable of creating new content, from text and images to music, through the use of large language models and generative adversarial networks.

linked_companies.name: NVIDIA CORP
linked_companies.description: Powers the development and deployment of large language models and generative artificial intelligence through foundational graphics processing units and comprehensive software ecosystems optimized for massive computational workloads.
linked_companies.evidence: NVIDIA functions as the foundational infrastructure layer for the Generative AI and LLM industry, distinguishing itself as the sole platform running every frontier AI model, including OpenAI's GPT-5.5, Google's Gemini, and Meta's MSL. The company's hardware strategy is directly driven by the capacity requirements for training and deploying these language models, demonstrated by the co-design and serving of advanced applications on its Blackwell architecture. To expand compute capabilities across the ecosystem, NVIDIA executes dedicated research and capital partnerships, recently directing portions of an $18.6 billion investment pool toward AI model makers like Anthropic. By securing deep hardware integrations and financially backing both proprietary and open-source foundation model builders, NVIDIA structurally enables the global hyperscale transition from classical machine learning to generative AI workloads.

linked_companies.name: MICROSOFT CORP
linked_companies.description: Drives the development and commercialization of generative AI by integrating large language models into its productivity applications and providing the underlying cloud infrastructure required to train and deploy advanced AI systems.
linked_companies.evidence: Microsoft drives Generative AI adoption through a dual approach, deploying proprietary, in-house models like MAI-Image-2 and MAI-Transcribe-1 alongside external models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and open-source developers on its Foundry platform. This integrated infrastructure has propelled the company's AI business to a $37 billion annual recurring revenue, accounting for approximately 11.1% of total corporate revenue. The company's market position is further solidified by the processing of over one trillion tokens for enterprise customers, the direct embedding of generative capabilities into applications like Copilot and Bing, and a foundational, royalty-free intellectual property partnership with OpenAI extending through 2032.

linked_companies.name: ALPHABET INC-CL A
linked_companies.description: Develops foundational large language models and generative artificial intelligence technologies, integrating these capabilities across its search, cloud infrastructure, and software ecosystem to power advanced reasoning and automated content generation.
linked_companies.evidence: Alphabet's core strategy relies on the rapid deployment of proprietary, multi-modal generative AI models, highlighted by recent releases such as Gemini 3.1 Pro, the Veo 3.1 Lite video model, and the open Gemma 4 model. This extensive portfolio drives massive ecosystem engagement, processing over 16 billion tokens per minute via direct APIs and fueling nearly 800% year-over-year revenue growth for cloud-based GenAI products. Supporting this widespread adoption is a centralized, multi-billion-dollar foundational R&D commitment led by Google DeepMind to advance frontier models and build new capabilities like the Project Genie world model. Consequently, these AI technologies are seamlessly embedded and monetized across Alphabet's enterprise and consumer platforms, including Vertex AI, Gemini Enterprise, and Google One premium subscriptions.

linked_companies.name: AMAZON.COM INC
linked_companies.description: Provides comprehensive cloud infrastructure and platform services for generative AI, featuring custom silicon for model training and inference, managed services like Amazon Bedrock for accessing large language models, and enterprise-grade AI assistants.
linked_companies.evidence: Amazon's integration of Generative AI and LLMs across AWS currently drives an AI revenue run rate exceeding $15 billion, sustained by a $43.2 billion quarterly capital expenditure directed toward AI cloud infrastructure. The company utilizes Amazon Bedrock as its central development platform, providing a stateful runtime environment for managed agents alongside access to leading models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, and Llama. Specialized generative tools are also actively deployed within core consumer segments, explicitly demonstrated by the retail assistant Rufus and the advertising system Creative Agent. This ecosystem is secured through extensive financial agreements, encompassing $50 billion in direct equity commitments to OpenAI, the proprietary development of Amazon Nova models, and an excess of $100 billion in backlog deals with Anthropic.

linked_companies.name: COREWEAVE INC-CL A
linked_companies.description: Delivers specialized, massive-scale GPU cloud infrastructure purpose-built to power the compute-intensive training and inference workloads required for large language models and generative artificial intelligence applications.
linked_companies.evidence: CoreWeave operates as the foundational computing infrastructure for major Generative AI and large language model (LLM) platforms, powering training and inference for nine of the ten leading AI developers outside of China. Recent Q2 2026 agreements emphasize this position, as the company secured a $21 billion capacity commitment from Meta, added Anthropic to support its Claude models, and financed extensive contracts for OpenAI and Cohere. These foundational labs, alongside AI-native application creators like Midjourney, Runway, and Cognition, drive intense compute demand to build and deploy leap-forward generative models. Providing the underlying cloud architecture for these AI pioneers dictates a significant share of CoreWeave's capital expenditure and accounts for nearly 30% of its $100 billion revenue backlog.

themes.name: Communication Tools
themes.description: Software and platforms enhancing real-time interaction through voice, video, text, and other digital channels.

linked_companies.name: TWILIO INC - A
linked_companies.description: Provides a comprehensive cloud communications platform featuring programmable APIs that enable developers to seamlessly integrate voice, messaging, video, and email capabilities into customer applications.
linked_companies.evidence: Twilio operates an omnichannel platform driven by messaging, voice, email, and video APIs that recently generated $1.4 billion in quarterly revenue. Communication channels form the core of its business, with messaging applications like SMS, WhatsApp, and RCS accounting for nearly 60% of total revenue and accelerating to 25% year-over-year growth alongside a 20% increase in voice revenue. The company restructured its dedicated go-to-market organization to optimize cross-selling across these channels while directing R&D investments to launch context-rich conversational intelligence capabilities. Processing billions of multi-channel transactions during peak periods like Cyber Week validates this infrastructure scale and underpins Twilio's market leadership recognitions from analysts including IDC, Omdia, and Gartner.

linked_companies.name: RINGCENTRAL INC-CLASS A
linked_companies.description: Provides cloud-based unified communications platforms that integrate voice, video meetings, team messaging, and contact center capabilities to facilitate seamless enterprise collaboration.
linked_companies.evidence: RingCentral's core operations are entirely defined by its cloud-based communication tools, with its omnichannel customer engagement platforms—spanning voice, text, and video—generating nearly 97% of its total revenue. Processing tens of billions of interactions annually through flagship offerings like RingEX and RingCX, the company maintains an established market position validated by leadership recognition from IDC and Omdia. To sustain this $2.7 billion annual recurring revenue business, RingCentral leverages a vast global workforce of specialized engineers and directs over $250 million annually into research and development to continuously advance its unified communications infrastructure.

linked_companies.name: ZOOM COMMUNICATIONS INC
linked_companies.description: Develops a comprehensive unified communications platform featuring video meetings, cloud telephony, and team chat to facilitate seamless digital collaboration across distributed workforces.
linked_companies.evidence: Zoom functions fundamentally as a pure-play provider of real-time digital communication platforms, deriving practically its entire revenue from voice, video, and text interaction software. The company's AI-first, open work platform facilitates this connectivity through an integrated suite of products including Zoom Meetings, Zoom Phone, and Zoom Team Chat. To sustain and advance these core tools, Zoom directly channels its workforce operations and major capital investments—such as a recent $227.9 million quarterly research and development expenditure—into its communication infrastructure. This specialized focus enables the platform to support hundreds of millions of user seats globally and execute large-scale enterprise deployments that replace legacy telecom solutions.

linked_companies.name: FIVE9 INC
linked_companies.description: Provides cloud-based contact center software that integrates omnichannel routing, artificial intelligence, and workforce optimization to facilitate and enhance enterprise customer communications.
linked_companies.evidence: Five9's core business fundamentally revolves around its cloud-based contact center solutions, which act as a real-time orchestration engine for enterprise communications. By seamlessly integrating voice, digital, and AI channels into a unified interface, the company's platform transforms customer service operations and enhances agent capabilities. This deep engagement with communication tools drives the vast majority of the company's financial performance, with software subscriptions and directly integrated telecom solutions accounting for approximately 94% of its total revenue. Furthermore, ongoing commitments—such as dedicating substantial R&D funding toward expanding these omnichannel capabilities—highlight the communication platform's central role as the flagship product serving over 3,000 enterprise customers.

linked_companies.name: BANDWIDTH INC-CLASS A
linked_companies.description: Powers cloud-based communication tools by providing a comprehensive suite of application programming interfaces for voice, messaging, and emergency services backed by a proprietary global network.
linked_companies.evidence: Bandwidth functions as a pure-play Communications Platform-as-a-Service (CPaaS) provider, meaning its foundational strategy and revenue base are entirely dependent on programmable communication APIs. In the second quarter of 2026, the company generated $150 million from cloud communications, with voice solutions and programmable messaging accounting for nearly three-quarters of its total quarterly top line. Operational resources and C-suite executives, including the Chief Product Officer and COO, are explicitly dedicated to managing this global communications cloud and its Maestro orchestration layer. By operating a scaled proprietary network, the company facilitates billions of real-time interactions globally and serves as the underlying infrastructure powering industry-leading unified communications and contact center platforms across more than 80 countries.
